title: initiative-portfolio-for-slo-runway-and-cross-team-escalation
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Define and ship an Initiative Portfolio view and automation that tracks SLO runway across grouped initiatives and provides automated cross-team escalation when aggregated error budget burn or projected miss thresholds are reached. This work focuses on product-side orchestration (UI, decision rules, experiment configuration) and the data contract with Telemetry/ENG for SLI ingestion and projection signals.

Problem statement: Teams today manage SLOs at the service or route level but lack a first-class way to group related initiatives (eg. serving runtime, routing fallbacks, console UX) into a portfolio that represents a single customer-facing reliability objective. This makes it hard to: 1) understand combined error-budget runway for an initiative spanning multiple teams; 2) automate escalation and throttle new launches when aggregated burn indicates risk; 3) expose an easy playbook for on-call and PMs to act.

Scope and deliverables:
- UI: Initiative Portfolio page in the Console that lists grouped initiatives, aggregate SLI/SLO metrics (current burn rate, 7d projection, runway in days), and per-initiative contribution.
- Rules engine: Configurable policies for automated escalation that can trigger: Slack notify, create incident placeholder, block new rollout tags, or flag for executive review when portfolio-level projected miss probability > threshold.
- Data contract: Specification (proto/JSON) for how ENG telemetry will emit per-route SLI slices and a projection payload (burn-rate, projection-horizon) to a new portfolio ingestion endpoint.
- Migration: Import tool to map existing SLOs/initiatives into portfolios with suggested groupings based on service tag heuristics and historical correlation.
- Runbook: Playbook templates and default escalation flows that teams can customize.

Success metrics:
- Product: 80% of reliability initiatives created in Cycle 53 use Portfolio grouping for rollouts.
- SLO outcomes: Reduce surprise SLA incidents associated with cross-team rollouts by 30% (measured by incidents that cite multi-service interactions).
- Developer time saved: average time-to-action on early-warning alerts reduced from 2.5 hours to <60 minutes.

Acceptance criteria:
- Feature gated behind "reliability_portfolio" feature flag.
- Console page shows accurate aggregated numbers within 5% of SRE's canonical ledger for a test dataset.
- Automated escalation rules fire and produce expected actions in staging (Slack message, incident creation).
- Import tool correctly suggests groupings with >=60% precision on 3 historical initiatives.
- End-to-end test (telemetry -> ingestion -> projection -> UI) runs in CI and is part of the release checklist.

Out of scope: fine-grained token-level cost analyses, dedicated capacity provisioning changes, and RBAC for enterprise isolation (these will be followups).
